Inglewood, California
  January 9, 2024

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
January 9, 2024, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01 p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor Butts, Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk;
  and
  Absent: None.

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item No. CS-1.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session Item
No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
of 2:00 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Gray, Padilla,
  Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any item
on the Agendas.

There was no response.
 January 9, 2024

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated January
  4, 2024, in the amount of $4,164,926.07, and dated December 15, 2023, in the amount of
  $8,277,961.33 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing
  Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers that said demands
  are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Agenda Item No. 3 was pulled for further discussion.

125  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Andrew Goosby, Jr. for alleged Personal Injury; Negligence, Discrimination, Civil
  Rights Violation on October 10, 2023.
  2. Lloyd Mosley for alleged Personal Injury; ADA Curb Violation on January 31, 2023.
  3. Rosario Salazar for alleged Property Damage; Fallen Tree Branch on September 18,
  2023.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby Reject Claims listed as A-1 through A-3. The motion was carried
  by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

160  COOPERATIVE PURCHASE AGREEMENT NO. 24-099 APPROVED – NEW
  TANGRAM, L.L.C. (TANGRAM). Staff report dated January 9, 2024, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members approve a four-month Cooperative
  Purchase Agreement with New Tangram, L.L.C. (Tangram), for the purchase and
  installation of furniture for the Morningside Park Library.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby approve Cooperative Purchase Agreement No. 24-099 in the
  not-to-exceed amount of $170,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

131.8  RESOLUTION NO. 24-27 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024
  OPERATING BUDGET. Staff report dated January 9, 2024, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members adopt a resolution amending the Fiscal
  Year 2023-2024 Operating Budget to include affordable housing funds for the costs of
  Contract Services and Special Expenses.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  Resolution No. 24-27 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 BUDGET TO
  APPROPRIATE $76,500 FOR MAINTENANCE AND OPERATIONS
  EXPENDITURES FOR THE AFFORDABLE HOUSING DIVISION

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
 January 9, 2024

160  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 24-098 APPROVED –
  AMS.NET, INC.; CITY-CONTROLLED CONTINGENCY APPROVED;
  RESOLUTION NO. 24-26 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024
  BUDGET. Staff report dated January 9, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor
  and Council Members award a contract and approve an agreement with AMS.Net, Inc. to
  install network infrastructure for the Morningside Park Library.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that the City
  Council does hereby: 1) Award contract and approve Agreement No. 24-098 in the amount
  of $71,228.42; 2) Approve a 10% City-Controlled Contingency in the amount of $7,123 for
  a total not-to-exceed project amount of $78,351.42; and 3) Adopt Resolution No. 24-26
  entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 BUDGET TO
  ALLOCATE MONEY FOR THE MORNINGSIDE PARK LIBRARY
  NETWORK INFRASTRUCTURE INSTALLATION PROJECT

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  PUBLIC HEARING SET – AN APPEAL OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION
  DENIAL FOR SPECIAL USE PERMIT TO ALLOW A MORTUARY IN AN
  APPROXIMATELY 4,200 SQUARE-FOOT ONE-STORY COMMERCIAL
  BUILDING. Staff report dated January 9, 2024, was presented requesting that the Mayor
  and Council Members set a public hearing to consider an appeal by J.D. Thompson
  (applicant) of the Planning Commission’s decision to deny a Special Use Permit to allow a
  mortuary in an approximately 4,200 square-foot one-story commercial building.

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing set for January 23, 2024, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

183&169  ORDINANCE NO. 24-04 INTRODUCED - AMENDING CHAPTER 3 OF THE
  INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE TO DESIGNATE CITY-OWNED PARKING
  FACILITIES AS PARKING METER ZONES, AND ESTABLISHING SPECIAL
  EVENT PARKING RATES AND FINES FOR ON-STREET AND OFF-STREET
  PARKING METER ZONES. Staff report dated January 9, 2024, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members introduce an ordinance designating
  City-owned Parking Facilities as Parking Meter Zones and establishing Special Event
  Parking Rates and fines for On-street and Off-street Parking Meter Zones.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 24-04 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA
  AMENDING CHAPTER 3 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE TO
  DESIGNATE CITY-OWNED PARKING FACILITIES AS PARKING
  METER ZONES, ESTABLISH VARIABLE SPECIAL EVENT PARKING
  METER RATES, AND ESTABLISH PARKING FINES FOR VIOLATIONS
  THEREOF

  was introduced by Council Member Morales.

132.9  CLOSED SESSION – POTENTIAL LITIGATION – LYDI SALAS CLAIM FOR
  DAMAGES. Closed Session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged; City Council
  Conference with Legal Counsel regarding potential litigation pursuant to Government Code
  Section 54956.9(d)(2); Lydi Salas Claim for Damages; Date of Loss: Dec 5, 2022.

  3
 January 9, 2024

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby approve the request for settlement. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  REPORTS – CITY MANAGER. City Manager Mark F. Weinberg welcomed
  Councilwoman Gray back to the dais and stated that it’s always nice to see her. He extended
  his deepest sympathies on behalf of all City employees to the Padilla family for the loss of
  one of the family’s matriarchs. He stated that as a part of a larger family, his thoughts and
  prayers continue to be with the Padilla family. The City Manager stated that this was the
  first meeting after the retirement of the previous City Manager, Artie Fields, and
  congratulated him on a successful 12-year tenure. He also added that it was almost unheard
  of for a City Manager to work 12 years; typically, it’s about 48 months in California.
  Additionally, he added that he believes it’s a testimony to his service and working for an
  outstanding Council.

  Furthermore, he added that if Artie Field were watching, he would hopefully be spending
  time with his family and probably feel out of sorts, not sitting on the dais in his seat. The
  City Manager discussed his tenure as an appointed City Manager and mentioned it was
  his third appointment to the seat he was serving. He mentioned how excited,
  optimistic, and enthusiastic about becoming a part of the transition into the next
  generation of leaders in the administrative office. Finally, he expressed his appreciation
  for the trust and confidence that the Mayor and Council Members had in him, adding that
  he would do everything he could to continue to have those characteristics.

126  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson wished everyone a Happy
  New Year. She expressed her pleasure in working with Mark F. Weinberg, interim city
  manager, again and stated that it's a different role, but it's great to be working alongside
  him. She also expressed her sincere condolences to Council Member Padilla and his  family
  for their loss. She stated that he and his family were in her prayers and to call her if he needed
  something because he was there when she lost her parents. She reported her  attendance at
  We Grow LA in connection with the Inglewood Clothing Store run by  Steve Cotton. She
  noted that they did a great job with their holiday giveaway. Also, she  reported attending the
  North Pole Toy Drive at the Serving Spoon, which was a huge  success because so many
  children were blessed with tons of toys.

  Additionally, she added her attendance at the Homegoing Celebration for Mr. Leonard
  Tibbs and expressed how delighted she was to see Council Member Gray back on the
  dais. She stated that Councilwoman Gray did a fantastic job sending Mr. Tibbs home, and
  everything was excellent, well-attended, and organized. She also mentioned that she was
  praying for Councilwoman Gray. Furthermore, she wished herself a Happy Birthday and
  stated that this was her first year without her mom and dad. Finally, she reminded residents that
  City Hall would be closed on Monday, January 15, 2024, in observance of Martin Luther King
  Jr.'s birthday.

114  APPOINTMENT TO THE HOUSING ADVISORY BOARD RATIFIED – AT
  LARGE. Mayor Butts appointed Stephanie Kimbrough to the Housing Advisory
  Commission for the term ending November 2026. The appointment was carried and ratified
  by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  4
 January 9, 2024

  Charlene Sanders, District 1 Resident, spoke about an issue she noticed on December
  23, 2023. She stated that she noticed water running in the yard next to her on Buckthorn, one of
  the main thoroughfares into SoFi Stadium. She also noted the water kept coming out, and it
  looked like a lake because it was running down the curbside. Charlene added  that  she
  witnessed feces coming out all over the place, and by December 26, 2023, the issue  had
  worsened. She mentioned calling the Inglewood Police Department (IPD) and Council
  Member Gray’s assistant. She also noted that IPD called her back and told her that they
  would send someone out. Charlene addressed Councilwoman Gray’s assistant, who  called
  her back when she returned from out of town. She called the Public Works  Department,
  which went to the location. She discussed how devastating it was to  witness what she saw,
  and every time people flushed their toilets, it spread everywhere. Charlene also discussed her
  concern about what was happening in the City of Inglewood  because some owners are not
  taking care of the places where tenants live. Finally, she  explained that there was a new
  company that had been taking care of the property, and  this was a result of gentrification.

  Council Member Gray left the dais at the hour of 2:23 p.m.

  MAYOR BUTTS COMMENTS. Mayor Butts read a thank you card from Dr. James
  Morris, Los Angeles County Superintendent, on behalf of the Inglewood Unified School District
  students and families. The card thanked the Mayor, Council Members, and the  City  of
  Inglewood Team for supporting students and families during the holiday season and for the
  generous donation of Target gift cards. Mayor Butts also read some of the notes and displayed
  the book which the students put together.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts recognized the retirement of
  Jeffrey Lewis, Senior Assistant City Attorney, and the return of Mark F. Weinberg, City
  Manager, and declared the meeting adjourned in the honor of Belen Maldonado, Mother-
  in-law of Council Member Alex Padilla, and Jakim Stewart, one of the owners of Drobe
  Stogies, at the hour of 2:35 p.m.

  Approved this ____ day of __________, 2024.
